compactRecord.td: The 'Giant of Provence' (1910m) rises in isolation above the Vaucluse plateau, its white limestone summit visible from 300km. A legendary Tour de France climb and the site of Petrarch's 1336 recreational ascent — one of the first recorded in Europe.

compactRecord.rs: One of Provence's great Roman sites — 15 hectares of Gallo-Roman city, a 2000-year-old bridge still in daily use, and a medieval citadel towering above.
compactRecord.td: France's largest Gallo-Roman open-air site — two vast excavated quarters (Puymin and Villasse) with intact mosaics, baths and a 6000-seat theatre still in use today, plus a 1st-century Roman bridge and a spectacular medieval perched upper town.

compactRecord.rs: France's northernmost AOC olive oil village — Tanche olives pressed here since the 14th century, a warm Provençal old town, and one of southern France's most beloved weekly markets.
compactRecord.td: The olive-oil capital of France, sheltered by the Baronnies mountains with one of the Drôme's mildest climates. The medieval Lanciers quarter, Romanesque bridge, AOC olive mills and Thursday market are celebrated across France.

compactRecord.rs: The 'linden capital of the world' — a sun-baked medieval market village ringed by Provence-style limestone peaks.
compactRecord.td: Charming medieval village in the Baronnies Provençales, surrounded by dramatic limestone peaks and world-renowned as the leading producer of linden blossom (tilleul). The midsummer flower market fills the arcaded square with intoxicating fragrance.
